subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — indemnity redlines, evidence checklist & kanban
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzales <maria.gonzales@asterion.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form — indemnity redlines, evidence checklist & kanban

Hi Maria —

Thanks again for walking through the high level terms yesterday. Per our call, attaching a clean redline of the MSA + order form R3 and a first-pass evidence checklist so we can align on operational handoffs if the IP indemnity trigger is invoked.

Quick summary of our asks/positions in the redline:
- Redwood accepts customer notice/cure obligations and will cooperate in defense; we propose narrow third-party claim definition limited to claims alleging that Customer Content infringes a third party patent/copyright.
- We cannot accept broad "generated output" indemnity without limits; proposed carve-ins for model-generated content tied to Customer Content + proof threshold.
- Cap remains as negotiated in order form; we propose keeping insurance offset language but clarifying sequence of obligations.

Please review the evidence checklist tab — it separates "technical artifacts" (request logs, model snapshot, training provenance) from procurement docs (purchase orders, license chain). We view the tech artifact lane as ops-owned; asking Asterion to confirm receipt SLA for evidence requests (we propose 7 business days for a first bundle).

I've created a short kanban board (link below) for the evidence triage flow — feel free to invite your ops/counsel.

Attachments: 20260809_Redline_MSA_Asterion_vNAF.docx (redline), evidence_checklist_v1.xlsx

Next steps:
1) Maria: high-level counsel read of proposed carveouts (today/Tuesday)
2) Kimberly: if counsel pushes on defense-control we expect to propose a hybrid approach — partial control with vendor-managed counsel for technical discovery (ETA Wed)
3) Ben/Grace: confirm commercial impact if Asterion requests wider coverage (estimate by Thursday)

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we want to keep the order form on the August cadence.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Commercial Legal | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Naomi —

Thanks for the materials and the clear separation of evidence types. Quick initial reactions from GC team:
- Asterion is okay narrowing third-party IP claims to content provided by the customer, but we need clearer language on derivative works produced by the model when those outputs are a direct function of uploaded Customer Content.
- Our primary ask is stronger defense-control: if a claim affects our customers materially we need the ability to take lead with counsel of our choosing; we are open to sharing costs and coordinating on technical discovery.
- Concerned about the 7 business day window for evidence; operations in regulated spaces may need up to 14 business days in some scenarios. Can Redwood accept a two-stage SLA: 7 business days for a first bundle (log extracts + custody manifest) and 14 business days for full technical artifacts unless expedited by a court order?

We reviewed the kanban board — procurement will invite our ops lead (Sanjay) to confirm escalation contacts.

Would you be available for a 30-min follow-up tomorrow afternoon to work through the defense-control wording?

Best,
Maria Gonzales
General Counsel | Asterion Systems
maria.gonzales@asterion.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 08:57:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — indemnity redlines, evidence checklist & kanban

Maria / Naomi —

Thanks Maria — useful surface-level asks. A few internal points from legal on defense-control and the two-stage SLA that we can propose in redline:

1) Defense-control — hybrid proposal (language I'll draft):
- If a third-party IP claim is solely about Customer Content, Asterion may elect to assume primary defense with counsel of its choice; Redwood will reasonably cooperate and may propose Redwood-nominated counsel for technical depositions where we bear technical cost.
- If the claim arises primarily from Redwood model architecture or training artifacts (Redwood Confidential), Redwood reserves the right to manage defense with Asterion participating.
- Joint control carve: where facts overlap we propose a quick escalation within 5 business days to senior GC/principal (names on kanban).

2) Evidence SLA — two-stage approach acceptable; revise wording to:
- Redwood to produce initial custody manifest and log extracts within 7 business days of notice request.
- Full technical artifacts delivered within 14 business days where feasible; if nonfeasible provide written remediation ETA and escalation path.

3) Generated-output carve — strongly recommend we map examples in an appendix (3-4 rows) to reduce ambiguity: e.g., simple restatements of Customer Content vs. model hallucinations trained on external corpora.

I'll put these edits into a redline and upload to the kanban under "Legal: Proposed Compromise". Naomi — Ben/Grace please flag any commercial headwinds to the two-stage SLA or hybrid defense approach before EOD Wed.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Maria / team —

Appreciate the quick reviews. Operationally from commercial / sales perspective:
- The hybrid defense-control is acceptable as a go-forward compromise so long as cost-sharing and escalation timelines are explicit. We cannot leave the budget open-ended for multi-month discovery.
- The two-stage SLA seems workable; if Asterion needs longer we can add an expedited request path (court order / injunction) that short-circuits the timeline subject to cost allocation.
- If counsel requests broader coverage for "generated output" we will need a clear threshold tied to material customer harm plus a negotiated uplift to the order form cap or a separate insurance carve. Grace, please prepare a quick estimate of potential uplift if Asterion insists on a broader output indemnity.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kimberly to post redline with hybrid defense-control language + updated SLA (today)
2) Naomi to share redline in kanban under Legal: Proposed Compromise and tag Maria + procurement
3) Maria to confirm whether Asterion accepts hybrid approach or needs a call
4) Grace to post commercial uplift estimate by EOD Thu

We should aim to lock the indemnity language this week so procurement can finish payment terms next week.

Best,
Ben Carter
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
